(2) The long title of this Order is "An Order to provide for security interests in personal property relating to the creation, perfection, registration, priority and of personal property securities and for matters connected therewith".

heading.en: Appointment of Registrar and other officers

text.en:
(1) The Minister shall, with the approval of His Majesty the Sultan and appoint a Registrar of Collateral Registry for the purposes of this Order.

(2) The Minister may appoint a Deputy Registrar and one or more Assistant Registrars to assist the Registrar in carrying out his functions and duties this Order.

(3) The Registrar may, subject to such conditions as he thinks fit, delegate to the Deputy Registrar or any Assistant Registrars any of his powers or functions this Order, except the power of delegation conferred by this subsection.

(4) The Registrar may continue to exercise any power conferred on him or any function under this Order notwithstanding the delegation of such or function under this subsection. Registry
There shall be established an office which is known as the Collateral the purposes of registrations under this Order. of personal property security

(2) The register shall - (a} be an electronic register; and

(b) operated at all times, unless the Registrar suspends the operation in accordance with section 9.

AGREEMENTS of security agreement
Except as otherwise provided by this Order or any other written law, a agreement is effective according to its terms. of col~ateral in security agreement

( 1) A security agreement is enforceable and a security interest created in of the collateral only if fa) a security agreement contains an adequate description of the which description may be generic or specific; {b) value is given by the secured party; and {c) the debtor has rights in the collateral.

(2) A description of the collateral is adequate if the collateral is described byfa) item, kind, type or category; {b) a statement that a security interest is taken in all of the debtor's and after-acquired property; or {c) a statement that a security interest is taken in all of the debtor's and after-acquired property except for specified items or kinds of property.

(3) For the purposes of subsection (2), a description of the collateral is if the collateral is described as consumer goods without specific reference to the item or kind of collateral.

(4) otherwise provided in this Order, a security interest in is enforceable against a third party, whether or not the security providing for the security interest contains a description of the

OF SECURITY INTERESTS of security interest

(1) A security interest is perfected when(a) the security interest is created; and

(b) either - \i) statement is registered in respect of the security

(ii) the secured party or another person on behalf of the secured has possession of the coliateral (except where result of seizure or repossession); or

(iii) the secured party or another person on behalf of the secured has control of the collateral that is a deposit account or security.

(2) (1) applies regardless of the order in which creation referred to in subsection ( 1 )(a) and either of the steps referred to in subsect~on ! 1)(b) occur.

(3) A security interest in cash other than cash proceeds may only be by possession by the secured party or a person acting on behalf of the party. of perfection

A security interest is continuously perfected if

(a) the security interest is perfected under this Order;

(b) the security interest is subsequently perfected in another way this Order; and

(c) there is no intervening period during which the security interest is
A security agreement may provide for security interests in after-acquired which shall be created without written consent by the debtor, unless the property is consumer goods.

Except as otherwise provided in this Order, a security interest in the that is dealt with or otherwise gives rise to proceeds shall (a} continue in the collateral unless the secured party expressly or authorised the dealing; and

(b) extend to the proceeds, but if the secured party enforces the security interest against both the collateral and the proceeds, the amount secured by security interest in collateral and the is limited to the value of the collateral at the date of the dealing that the proceeds_

heading.en: Continuous perfection of security interests in proceeds

text.en:
A security interest in proceeds is continuously perfected if the security in the original collateral is perfected by registration of a financing that contains a description of the original collateral, if the proceeds - (a} are of a kind that is within the description of the original or

(b) are cash proceeds.

heading.en: Temporary perfection of security interests in proceeds in other cases

text.en:
( 1) the proceeds are not cash proceeds and not within the the collateral in the financing statement as referred to in section 16, a security interest in the proceeds shall be temporarily perfected within 10 days after the proceeds arose.

(2) If the secured party does not perfect the security interest by amending the financing statement to include the non-conforming proceeds within the 10 days, the security interest in the proceeds will become unperfected.

DARUSSALAM GOVERNMENT GAZETTE Temporary perfection of security interests in negotiable instruments or investment securities

A security interest in a negotiable instrument or an investment security that is perfected by possession shall remain perfected within 10 working days after the party made the negotiable instrument or investment security available to the debtor for the purposes of sale, exchange, presentation, collection, renewal or of a transfer. Temporary perfection of security interests in negotiable documents of title or goods

A security interest in a negotiable document of title or goods held by a that are not covered by a negotiable document of title or goods shall be perfected within 10 working days after the secured party made the document of title or goods available to the debtor, if{a} the security interest was perfected by possession; and {b) the secured party delivered the negotiable document of title or for the purposes of sale, exchange, loading, unloading, storing, manufacturing, processing, packaging or otherwise dealing with the goods in preparation for their sale or exchange. .

heading.en: Perfection where goods in hands of bailee

text.en: A security interest in goods in the possession of a bailee may be perfected when{a} the security interest has been created and a financing statement to the goods is registered; (bJ possession of a negotiable document of title to the goods has been to the secured party; or {c) the bailee has issued a document of title in the name of the party or holds the goods on behalf of the secured party. Security interests in crops

(1) as otherwise provided in this Order, a security interest may be and perfected in crops and continue as such before they are planted while and afterwards when cut or separated from the soil.

(2) A security interest in crops shall only be created with the consent of the mortgagee or lessor under a lease with the duration of not more than 3 years.

(3) No perfected security interest in crops shall be extinguished or affected by a subsequent sale, lease, mortgage or other encumbrance of or on the land on which the crops are growing.

BETWEEN SECURITY INTERESTS of security interests generally

heading.en: Priority of security interests in same collateral

text.en:
( 1) Where the Order does not provide another method for determining between security interests in the same collateral - fa} a perfected security interest shall have priority over an security interest; {b) priority between perfected security interests shall be determined by the order of whichever of the following first occurs in relation to a security interest -

(i) the registration of a financing statement;

(ii) the secured party, or another person acting on behalf of the party, taking possession of the collateral (except possession is a result of seizure or repossession J; or

(iii) the secured party, or another person acting on behalf of the party, acquiring control of the collateral; and {c) priority between unperfected security interests in the same collateral shall be determined by the order of creation of the security [2) For the purposes of subsection (1), a security interest that is first in one manner and later perfected in another manner without a break in perfection is continuously perfected and retains its priority from the date of its original perfection.

(3) Subject to section 15, the priority of a security interest in original collateral shall also be the priority with respect to its proceeds.

heading.en: Transfer of security interests does not affect priority

text.en: A security interest that is transferred shall have the same priority as it had at the time of the transfer. Voluntary subordination of security interests

(1) A secured party may, in a security agreement or otherwise, its security interest to any other interest.

(2) No agreement to subordinate the security interest shall adversely affect of a person who is not a party to the agreement.

(3) An agreement to subordinate a security interest shall be effective terms between the parties and may also be enforced by a third if the third party is the person for whose benefit the agreement is intended. of security interests to all advances
A security interest shall have the same priority in respect of all advances, future advances. of purchase money security interests in collateral etc. or its proceeds

heading.en: Priority of purchase money security interests in collateral etc. or its

text.en:
(1) A security interest in accounts receivable that is given for new value have priority over a purchase money security interest in the accounts proceeds of inventory if the security interest in the accounts receivable is registered before the purchase money security interest in the

(2) In this section, "new value" means value other than antecedent debt or

( 1) A security interest m the collateral that becomes an accession shall in the accession.

(2) If a security interest is perfected when the collateral becomes an the security interest remains perfected in the accession. Priority of security interests in goods before they become accessions

heading.en: of security interests in processed or commingled goods

text.en: A security interest in goods that is created at the time when the goods an accession shall have priority over a claim to the goods as an accession made by a person with an interest in the whole.

heading.en: Continuation of security interests in processed or commingled goods

text.en: A perfected security interest in goods that subsequently becomes part of a or mass shall continue as a perfected security interest in the product or mass if the goods are manufactured, processed, assembled, or commingled in such a way that their identity is lost in the product or mass.

heading.en: Limit on value of priority of processed or commingled goods

text.en: If more than .one security interest is perfected in the goods before they part of a product or mass, the security interests rank equally in to the value of the goods at the time they became part of the product Priority where more than one security interest continues in processed or commingled goods

(1) A perfected security interest continuing in the product or mass shall have priority over an unperfected security interest continuing in the same or mass.

(2) If more than one unperfected security interest continues in the same or mass, each unperfected security interest shall be entitled to share in the product or mass according to the ratio that the obligation secured by the security interest bears to the sum of the obligations secured by all security interests in the same product or mass.

DARUSSALAM GOVERNMENT GAZETTE Priority of purchase money security interests in goods that continue in processed or commingled goods

Notwithstanding section 32, a perfected purchase money security interest that continues in a product or mass shall have priority over (a} a non-purchase money security interest in the goods that in the product or mass; and

(b) a non-purchase money security interest in the product or mass by the same debtor. of security interests in transferred collateral

heading.en: Rights of debtor may be transferred

text.en:
( 1) The rights of a debtor in collateral may be transferred despite a the security agreement prohibiting transfer or declaring a transfer to be a default [2) No transfer by the debtor shall prejudice the rights of the secured party the security agreement, including the right to treat a prohibited transfer as an act of default.

(3) In this section, "transfer" includes a sale, the creation of a security or a transfer under judicial enforcement proceedings. General priority of security interests in transferred collateral over security interests granted

Where a debtor transfers an interest in the collateral that, at the time of the transfer, is subject to a perfected security interest, that security interest shall have over any other security interest granted by the transferee. Transfer of debtor's interest in collateral with prior consent of secured party

(1) If a security interest is perfected by registration and the debtor part of its interest in the collateral, the security interest in the collateral shall remain perfected against such collateral and, if the interest extends to after-acquired property, the security interest in the collateral shall remain perfected against any collateral that the acquires within 15 days.

(2) The security interest shall not be perfected with respect to the acquired by the transferee after the expiration of the 15 day period the secured party registers a financing statement naming the transferee as the debtor.

PRIORITY RULES

heading.en: Lien has priority over security interests relating to same goods

text.en: A possessory lien arising out of materials or services provided in respect of that are subject to a security interest in the same goods shall have priority over that security interest iffa} the materials or services relating to the lien were provided in the course of business; fb} the lien has not arisen under any written law that provides that the lien does not have the priority; and {c} the person who provided the materials or services did not, at the time the person provided those materials or know that the agreement relating to the goods contained a provision prohibiting the creation of a lien by the debtor.

heading.en: Transferee takes money free of security interest

text.en: A transferee of money takes the money free of a security interest unless the acts in collusion with the debtor in violating the rights of a secured

heading.en: Priority of creditor who receives payment of debt

text.en: A creditor who receives payment of a debt owing by a debtor through any system shall receive the payment free of a security interest whether or not the creditor had knowledge of the security interest at the time of the payment. Priority of purchaser of negotiable instrument, document of title, chattel paper and security

A purchaser of a negotiable instrument, document of title, chattel paper or certificate shall have priority over a perfected security interest in the instrument, document of title, chattel paper or security certificate if the purchaser - fa} gave value; fb} acquired the negotiable instrument, document of title, chattel or security certificate without knowledge that the transaction is a of the security agreement to which the security interest relates; and

DARUSSALAM GOVERNMENT GAZETTE

(c) took possession of the negotiable instrument, document of title, paper or security certificate. Priority of interests on assignment of account receivable or non-negotiable chattel paper

(1) The rights of an assignee of an account receivable or non-negotiable paper shall be subject to - {a) the terms of the contract between the account debtor and the and any defence or claim arising from the contract or a closely contract; and

(b) any other defence or claim of the account debtor against the assignor (including a defence by way of a right of set-off} that accrues before the account debtor receives notification of the assignment.

(2) In this section, "assignee" includes a transferee or other secured party.

heading.en: Judgment creditor has priority over unperfected security interests

text.en:
(1) The interest of a judgment creditor in any collateral shall have priority over any security interest in the same collateral if the security interest is not at the time of execution.

(2) "time of execution" means

(a) if the collateral is seized by or on behalf of a judgment creditor, the time of seizure; or

(b) in any other case, the time when a charging order or a garnishee is served on the person holding some property for or on behalf of the

heading.en: Buyer or lessee takes collateral free of unperfected security interests

text.en: A buyer or lessee of collateral who acquires the collateral for value shall take the collateral free of an unperfected security interest in the collateral. Buyer or lessee of goods sold or leased in ordinary course of business takes goods free of

A buyer of goods sold in the ordinary course of business of the seller and a lessee of goods leased in the ordinary course of business of the lessor shall take the goods free of a security interest created by the seller or lessor unless the buyer or lessee knows that the sale or lease constitutes a breach of the security under which the security interest was created. may register financing statement

A person may register a financing statement which shall contain the particulars - (a} if the debtor is -

(i) an individual, the name, address and date of birth;

(ii) an unregistered company -

(A) the name and address of the company; and

(B) the name, job title and contact details of the person on its behalf;

(iii) a registered company, a unique number assigned to it on its

(b) if the secured party is -

(i) an individual, the name, address and date of birth;

(ii) an unregistered company, the name and address of the or

(iii) a registered company, a unique number assigned to it on its

(c) a description of the collateral; and

(d) any other particulars as the Registrar may require to be contained in the financing statement.

heading.en: Financing statement or financing change statement not registered

text.en:
A financing statement or financing change statement shall not be registered if(a) it is not submitted in the manner and form as the Registrar may that enables the information to be entered directly by electronic into the register; or

DARUSSALAM GOVERNMENT GAZETTE {b) the prescribed fee has not been paid to the Registrar, unless for its payment have been made in accordance with the of financing statement

(1) A financing statement shall be registered at the time a registration date and time are assigned to it by the Registry, and it shall not be against third parties until it is searchable in the register.

(2) A financing statement may be registered before or after a security is concluded.

(3) A financing statement may relate to one or more security agreements.

( 1 J A verification statement shall, as soon as reasonably practicable after a statement has been registered, be given to the person who submitted the financing statement for registration.

(2) A copy of the verification statement shall be given to the debtor by the party who registered a financing statement, or on whose beha1f a statement has been registered, within 15 working days after the statement is received, unless the debtor has waived in writing the to receive it. to register financing statement or financing change statement

heading.en: Authorisation to register financing statement or financing change statement

text.en:
(1) A debtor who enters into a security agreement authorise the of a financing statement and any amendments thereto.

(2) The debtor may also authorise registration of a financing statement to the conclusion of a security agreement and such authorisation shall be by debtor. of registration

( 1) The validity of the registration of a financing statement shall not be by a defect, irregularity, omission or error unless the defect, irregularity, or error is seriously misleading.

(2) If there is a seriously misleading defect, irregularity, omission or error in{a) the identifier of a debtor; or

(b) the serial number of the collateral, if so assigned, the registration shall be invalid. j3J If it is alleged that a defect, irregularity, omission or error is seriously misleading, it is not necessary to prove that any person was actually misled by it.

(4) An incorrect description of certain collateral shall not render the registration invalid with respect to other collateral sufficiently described in the statement. of registration

Except as otherwise provided in this Order, a registration of a financing shall be valid until (a} the expiration of the term specified in the financing statement; (bJ the expiration of 10 years commencing on the date on which and at the time at which the financing statement was registered; or

(c) · when the financing statement has been discharged before the the relevant period referred to in this section, is the earlier period. of registration

A registration may be renewed by registering a financing change statement at any time before the expiration of the registration, unless the period of time is until - {a) the expiration of the new term specified in the financing change or

(b) the expiration of 10 years commencing on the date on which and at the time at which the financing change statement was registered, is the earlier period. of transfer of perfected security interests

heading.en: Registration of transfer of perfected security interests

text.en:
( 1) If a secured party transfers a security interest perfected by registration, the transferred security interest shall remain effective.

(2) The transferee is not required to amend the registration that names the as the secured party or to register a new financing statement against

DARUSSALAM GOVERNMENT GAZETTE of subordinated security interests

If a secured party has subordinated a security interest to the interest of person, a financing change statement may be registered to disclose the at any time before the expiration of the registration. or discharge of registration

( 1) An amendment to or discharge of a registration may be made by the party by registering a financing change statement at any time before the expiration of the registration.

(2) An amendment to a registration -

(a) to add collateral; {b) to add a new debtor; or {c) to modify the maximum amount of the secured obligation, is only effective from the date of registration of the financing change statement. of registration relating to consumer goods

heading.en: Discharge of registration relating to consumer goods

text.en: If a registration covers consumer goods, the secured party shall discharge the registration within 15 working days after all obligations under the security creating the security interest are performed, unless the registration lapses before the expiration of the period. may demand registration of financing change statement

heading.en: Debtor may demand registration of financing change statement

text.en:
(1) prejudice to section 56, the debtor may demand in writing to the secured party to amend or discharge the registration where

(a) all of the obligations under the security agreement to which the registration relates have been performed and there is no commitment to make future advances; {b) the secured party has agreed to release part of the collateral in the registration; {c) the collateral described in the registration includes an item or kind of property that is not collateral under a security agreement between the party and the debtor; {d) no security agreement exists between the parties; and {e) the security interest is extinguished in accordance with this Order. (2} On receipt of the demand submitted under subsection {1), the secured shall register, within 15 working days, a financing change statement {a} discharging the registration with respect to matters described in l(a},(d} or (e};

(b) amending or discharging the registration as to reflect the terms of the agreement in a case within subsection (l){b}; or {c} amending the registration to release some property that is no longer collateral or that was never collateral under a security agreement the secured party and the debtor referred to in subsection 1(c}. {3) A secured party shall not charge any fee on the demand by the debtor subsection ( 1).

(4) If a secured party fails to comply with subsection {1), the debtor may to the Court to issue an order amending or discharging the registration, as may be. order to amend or discharge

heading.en: Court order to amend or discharge

text.en:
{1) The Court may, on application by the debtor under section 57(4), order the registration to be amended or discharged.

(2) The Court may make any other order as it thinks proper for the of giving effect to an order under subsection ! 1 J. {3) The Registrar shall amend or discharge a registration in accordance with the order of the Court under subsection { 1) as soon as reasonably practicable receiving the or.der. in register

( 1) A person may search the register as to (a} the unique identifier of the debtor; {b} the serial number of the collateral, if so assigned; and

(c) the registration number assigned to the registration.

(2) A search in the register may be carried out without assigning any for the search. on registration and search

A person who submits a registration or carries out a search in the register with a frivolous, malicious or criminal purpose or intent is guilty of an offence.

DARUSSALAM GOVERNMENT GAZETTE Search certificate as evidence

The Registry may, on request and payment of the prescribed fee, issue a certificate which shall be conclusive evidence of the existence of information in the Registry as to the date and time of the issuance.

OF SECURITY INTERESTS of this Part

( 1) This Part applies to all security interests, except those created or for by

(a) an outright transfer of an account receivable or chattel paper;

(b) an operating lease that does not secure payment or performance of an obligation; or

(c) a commercial consignment that does not 'secure payment or of an obligation.

(2) This Part does not apply to remedies and measures provided in the Insolvency Order, 2015.

(3) The parties to a security agreement may contract out of sections 63, 64, 79, 83 and 84.

(1) If the debtor is in default, a secured party may -

(a) take possession of a collateral; or

(b) without removal, render the collateral unusable under section 64.

(2) A secured party may proceed under this section -

(a) to judicial process; or

(b) without judicial process, if the debtor does not resist the removal of the collateral.

(3) The commencement of enforcement requires registration of the form which shall identify

(a) the debtor; fb) the secured party; and

(c) the collateral against which enforcement is sought.

(4) A prior notice to the debtor is not required for the secured party to or render the collateral unusable under this section.

heading.en: Secured party may render collateral unusable

text.en:
(1) A secured party with priority over all other secured parties may render unusable under section 63 if the collateral is of a kind - fa} that cannot be readily removed from the premises of the debtor; or

(b) for which adequate storage facilities are not readily available.

(2) If subsection (1) applies, the secured party may dispose of the collateral on the premises of the debtor: that it shall not cause the person in possession of the premises, if than the debtor, any greater inconvenience than is necessary. Secured party may apply certain collateral in satisfaction of secured obligation

heading.en: Secured party may apply certain collateral m satisfaction of secured

text.en:
(1) Notwithstanding section 63, if the debtor is in default, a secured party with priority over all other secured parties may collect and apply an account investment security, money or negotiable instrument taken as the satisfaction of the obligation secured by the security interest.

(2) otherwise agreed, the secured party may notify the account and collect payment. risk

(1) Notwithstanding section 63, a secured party may take possession of the with or without leave of the Court, and sell the collateral when fa) the debtor is in default under the security agreement; and fb} the collateral is at risk.

(2) In subsection ( 1). collateral is at risk if the secured party has reasonable grounds to believe that the collateral has been or will be destroyed, damaged, endangered, disassembled, removed, concealed, sold or otherwise disposed of contrary to the provisions of the security agreement.

( 1) The collateral may be disposed of by the secured party in its existing condition or after repair, process or preparation for disposition.

(2) The cost of the repair, process or preparation may be included in the expenses of enforcement.

heading.en: Duty of secured party selling collateral
Power of sale applies to document of title and related goods

text.en: If the collateral is a document of title, the power of sale provided by section 66 applies to the document of title and to the goods to which it relates.
A secured party may effect a sale of the collateral under section 66 by public tender, private sale or any other method as may be provided in the security agreement.

heading.en: Buyer of collateral takes free of security interests

text.en: The buyer of the collateral in a sale under section 70 shall take it free of any interest.

heading.en: Secured party to give statement of account to debtor

text.en:
If collateral is sold by a secured party under section 70, the secured party within 15 working days after the sale of the collateral, give the persons to in section 68 a statement of account in writing, showing - (a} the amount of the gross proceeds of sale; (bf the amount of the costs and expenses of the sale; and

(c) the balance owing by the secured party to the debtor, or by the to the secured party, as the case may be.

heading.en: Secured party selling collateral to pay prior ranking secured parties

text.en: A secured party who has sold the collateral under section 70 shall, before applying the net proceeds of the sale towards the satisfaction of the debt or other secured by the security interest of the secured party, apply the net of the sale towards the reasonable costs and expenses of the sale.

(1) For the purposes of this Order, there is a surplus when the net recovered on disposition of the collateral under this Part exceeds the owed by the debtor to the secured party.

(2) If the secured party has retained the collateral pursuant to section 77 or sold the collateral under section 70, as the case may be, the secured party shall pay the following persons the amount of any surplus in the following order - (a} any person who has a subordinate security interest perfected by in the order of the priority;

(b) any other person who has given the secured party notice that that claims an interest in the collateral; and

(c) the debtor.

(3) In subsection (1), "net proceeds" means net proceeds of the sale after deducting the reasonable costs and expenses of the secured party of, and incidental to, taking possession of, holding, storing, repairing, maintaining, valuing, and preparing the sale of, and selling, the collateral. may be paid into Court

heading.en: Surplus may be paid into Court

text.en: The secured party may pay the surplus into Court if there is a question as to who is entitled to receive payment under section 75. of secured party to retain collateral

heading.en: Proposal of secured party to retain collateral

text.en:
(1) A secured party with priority over all other secured parties may, after propose to retain the collateral in satisfaction of the obligation secured by it.

(2) The secured party shall give notice of the proposal to the persons to in section 68.

heading.en: Persons entitled to notice may object to proposal

text.en: The secured party shall sell the collateral under section 70 if a person who is entitled to a notice under section 71 and whose interest in the collateral would be adversely affected by the proposal of the secured party to retain the collateral gives to the secured party a notice of objection within 10 working days after receiving the notice referred to in section 77. Person making objection may be requested by secured party to prove interest

heading.en: making objection may be requested by secured party to prove

text.en: (1) The secured party may request a person, other than the debtor, who objects to provide proof of the interest of the person. (2} If the person to whom subsection (1) applies does not provide proof 10 working days after the request of the secured party, the secured party may proceed as if no objection were received from the person. Position where persons entitled to notice do not object to retention of collateral by secured

( 1 J If no notice of objection is received, the secured party shall, at the the 10 day period referred to in section 79

(a) be deemed to have irrevocably elected to take the collateral in the obligation secured by it; and

(b) be entitled to hold or dispose of the collateral free from all rights and interests of the debtor and of any person entitled to receive notice section 71(1).

(2) All security interests in the collateral that are subordinate to the interest of the secured party referred to in subsection (1) shall be extinguished. Secured party shall not damage goods when removing accession

(1) A secured party who is entitled to repossess an accession under section 63 shall remove the ac"cession from the whole in a manner that causes no greater to the other goods or that puts the person in possession of the whole to no greater inconvenience than is necessary for the removal of the accession.

(2) other than a debtor, who has an interest in the other goods at the time the goods become an accession shall be entitled to reimbursement for any damage to the interest of that person in the other goods caused by the removal of the accession.

(3) Any reimbursement payable under subsection (2) shall not include reimbursement for a reduction in the value of the property caused by the removal of the accession or by the necessity of the replacement of the accession.

(4) A person entitled to reimbursement under this section may refuse permission to remove the accession until the secured party has given adequate security for the reimbursement.

heading.en: Secured party to provide certain information relating to security interests

text.en:
(1) A debtor may request the secured party to send or make available to any specified person, at an address specified by the debtor making the request, any of the following information - {a) a summary of a security agreement that creates or provides for a interest held by the secured party in the personal property of the {b) a statement in writing of the amount of the indebtedness and of the terms of payment of the indebtedness; {c) a written approval or correction of an itemised list of personal indicating which items are collateral, unless the security interest is over all of the personal property of the debtor; or {d) a statement of account indicating the payoff amount needed to fully satisfy the secured obligation.

(2) A secured party shall comply with the request made under

(1) within 10 working days of its receipt, unless the secured party has been exempted under subsection (5).

(3) If, without reasonable excuse, the secured party fails to comply with the request within the specified period, the debtor making the request may apply to the Court for an order requiring the secured party to comply with the request.

(4) If the request is made and the secured party no longer has an interest in the obligation secured or collateral covered by the registration, the secured shall send or make available to the debtor the name and address of the immediate successor in interest or transferee and, if known, the latest successor in interest or transferee.

(5) The Court may, on application by a secured party, make an order to exempt the secured party from complying with subsections (1) and (2L in whole or may extend the time for compliance if the Court is satisfied that, in the circumstances, it would be unreasonable for the secured party to comply with the request.

(6) A secured party who is required to respond to the request may charge the debtor the reasonable costs for providing the information.

(7) A debtor shall be entitled to receive a reply without charge once every 3 months.

(8) If the secured party fails to comply with an order of the Court made subsection (3L the Court may (a} issue an order -

(1) The Registrar or any person authorised by him in writing may compound any offence against this Order by collecting from the person reasonably suspected of having committed that offence a sum of money not exceeding $1,000.

(2) On payment of such sum of money, no further proceedings shall be taken against such person in respect of the offence. by body corporate

(1) If a body corporate commits an offence under this Order, any person who at the time of the commission of the offence was a director, manager, secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate or was purporting to act in any such capacity or was in any manner or to any extent responsible for the management of any of the affairs of the body corporate or was assisting in such management -

(a) may be charged severally or jointly in the same proceedings with the body corporate; and

(b) if the body corporate is found to have committed the offence, shall be deemed to have committed that offence unless, having regard to the nature of his functions in that capacity and to all circumstances, he proves

(i) that the offence was committed without his knowledge, consent or connivance; and

(ii) that he had taken all reasonable precautions and exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence.

(2) If any person would be liable under this Order to any punishment or for his act, omission, neglect or default, he shall be liable to the same punishment or penalty for every such act, omission, neglect or default of any or agent of his, or of the employee of the agent, if the act, omission, neglect or default was committed

(a) by that person's employee in the course of his employment;

(b) by the agent when acting on behalf of that person; or

(c) by the employee of the agent in the course of his employment by the agent or otherwise on behalf of the agent acting on behalf of that person. effect
